name: MBrickz FM Schedule
author: MBrickz

sections.description:
MBrickz FM Schedule is a lightweight radio schedule management plugin for WordPress.

Create, manage, and display your radio shows directly from your WordPress dashboard. The plugin provides a customizable, responsive schedule with automatic live status updates, show countdowns, and a public JSON interface for compatible external services such as ET-HOST.

Manage your schedule in one place without having to maintain separate schedules for your website and radio chat.

Features

  • Dedicated radio show management in the WordPress dashboard.
  • Classic editor for creating and editing show descriptions.
  • Show date, start time, and end time.
  • Support for shows that continue past midnight.
  • DJ or presenter name and music genre.
  • Show covers and presenter avatars from the WordPress media library.
  • Live preview of the show card directly in the editor.
  • Responsive schedule display for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.
  • Chronological sorting by show date and start time.
  • Configurable pagination through plugin settings and shortcode parameters.
  • Option to display all available shows without pagination.
  • Automatic live status updates when scheduled shows begin.
  • Live status indicator with a subtle pulsing red dot.
  • Automatic removal of finished shows from the frontend without reloading the page.
  • Dynamic schedule and pagination updates across all schedule pages.
  • Optional global countdown to the next upcoming show.
  • Individual countdown shortcodes for specific radio shows.
  • Countdown display with days, hours, minutes, and seconds.
  • Automatic singular and plural countdown unit labels.
  • Server-synchronized countdowns and schedule status updates.
  • Support for reduced motion preferences.
  • Customizable background, text, accent, secondary text, and border colors.
  • Adjustable border radii for show cards, covers, and presenter avatars.
  • Restore default design settings at any time.
  • Theme-based font inheritance in the frontend.
  • Extended dashboard overview with show covers, dates, times, presenters, genres, and schedule status.
  • Sortable columns in the show overview.
  • Show IDs and copyable individual countdown shortcodes in the show overview.
  • Automatic return to the show overview after publishing a new show.
  • Public, read-only JSON REST API.
  • JSON format designed for compatibility with ET-HOST.
  • Translation-ready, with translations managed through WordPress.org.
  • Optional complete removal of plugin data on uninstall.

Display your schedule

Add the following shortcode to any page or post:

[mbrickzfm_schedule]

The shortcode uses the pagination settings configured under Schedule > Settings.

By default, pagination is enabled and five shows are displayed per page.

To override the number of shows per page:

[mbrickzfm_schedule limit="3"]

To display all available shows without pagination:

[mbrickzfm_schedule pagination="false"]

To enable pagination independently of the global settings:

[mbrickzfm_schedule pagination="true"]

To enable pagination with a specific number of shows per page:

[mbrickzfm_schedule limit="3" pagination="true"]

Explicit shortcode parameters override the corresponding global plugin settings.

Supported limits range from 1 to 100 shows per page.

When pagination is disabled, the limit parameter is ignored and all available shows are displayed.

The shortcode supports the WordPress block editor through the Shortcode block.

Configure pagination

Navigate to Schedule > Settings and locate the Schedule Pagination section.

The following settings are available:

  • Shows per Page: Number of shows displayed on each page.
  • Pagination: Enable or disable schedule pagination.

The default number of shows per page is five.

Pagination is enabled by default.

When pagination is disabled, all current and upcoming shows are displayed on a single page.

Pagination is automatically updated when scheduled shows end, including when the finished show is located on another schedule page.

If the currently displayed schedule page is no longer available, the schedule automatically displays the last available page.

Explicit shortcode parameters take precedence over the global settings.

Automatic live show status

The frontend schedule automatically updates the status of scheduled radio shows.

Before a show begins, its scheduled date and broadcast times are displayed.

When the scheduled start time is reached, the date and time display is replaced by a Live now indicator with a pulsing red dot.

When the scheduled end time is reached, the show is automatically hidden from the frontend schedule.

The schedule and pagination are subsequently refreshed in the background without requiring a full page reload.

The live status feature works independently of the global countdown setting.

The plugin respects the visitor’s reduced motion preference by disabling the pulsing animation when reduced motion is requested.

The live status is based on the configured schedule, not on the actual status of an audio stream.

Global show countdown

The optional global countdown displays the remaining time until the next scheduled radio show begins.

To enable the global countdown, navigate to Schedule > Settings and locate the Show Countdown section.

Enable the Global Countdown option.

The countdown is displayed below the schedule and its pagination, if applicable.

Only one global countdown is displayed per schedule shortcode.

The countdown always targets the next upcoming show, independently of the currently displayed schedule page.

The countdown includes:

  • Show title.
  • Presenter name, when available.
  • Scheduled show date and start time.
  • Remaining days, hours, minutes, and seconds.

When the target show begins, the global countdown automatically switches to the next upcoming show, if available.

If no upcoming shows are available, the global countdown is hidden.

The global countdown is disabled by default.

Individual show countdowns

Individual countdowns can be displayed independently of the main schedule using the following shortcode:

[fmsched_cnd id="123"]

Replace 123 with the ID of the desired radio show.

The show ID and its individual countdown shortcode are available in the radio show overview in the WordPress dashboard.

Before the scheduled start time, the shortcode displays a countdown to the selected show.

During the scheduled broadcast time, the countdown changes to a Live now display with a pulsing red dot and the scheduled end time.

After the scheduled show ends, the countdown is automatically hidden.

Individual countdowns work independently of the global countdown setting.

Multiple individual countdowns can be displayed on the same page.

Countdown labels automatically switch between singular and plural forms according to the displayed value.

Both global and individual countdowns use the configured schedule design and inherit the font family of the active WordPress theme.

Customize your design

Navigate to Schedule > Settings to customize the appearance of your schedule and countdowns.

Available design settings include:

  • Background color.
  • Text color.
  • Accent color.
  • Secondary text color.
  • Border color.
  • Show card border radius.
  • Cover border radius.
  • Presenter avatar border radius.

The frontend inherits its font family from your active WordPress theme.

The default design can be restored at any time.

Live editor preview

The radio show editor includes a live preview of the show card.

Changes to the title, description, date, times, genre, presenter, cover, and avatar are reflected in the preview without saving the show first.

The preview uses the configured schedule colors and border radii. Fonts and some layout details may differ from the public website because the preview is displayed inside the WordPress administration area.

JSON REST API

MBrickz FM Schedule provides a public, read-only REST API endpoint:

/wp-json/mbrickzfm/v1/schedule

The endpoint returns current and upcoming published shows in chronological order.

The JSON response contains a list named “shows”.

Each show contains the following required fields:

  • date
  • from
  • to
  • title

The following fields are included when available:

  • dj
  • cover
  • avatar

The date format is YYYY-MM-DD. Times are provided in HH:MM format using the WordPress site timezone.

The JSON endpoint is independent of frontend pagination and returns all valid, current and upcoming published shows.

Drafts, password-protected shows, incomplete shows, and finished shows are excluded.

The complete endpoint URL is available under Schedule > Settings.

Countdown REST API

The plugin provides an additional public, read-only REST API endpoint for countdown synchronization:

/wp-json/mbrickzfm/v1/countdown

The endpoint provides the current server timestamp and information about the next upcoming show when the global countdown is enabled.

To retrieve countdown information for a specific radio show, use the id parameter:

/wp-json/mbrickzfm/v1/countdown?id=123

Replace 123 with the ID of the desired radio show.

Individual show countdown requests are independent of the global countdown setting.

The frontend uses this endpoint to synchronize countdowns and schedule status updates with the server clock.

The countdown endpoint does not replace or modify the existing JSON schedule endpoint used by compatible external services.

ET-HOST integration

The JSON interface is designed to match the documented JSON schedule format supported by ET-HOST.

Copy the JSON endpoint URL from the plugin settings and configure it as an external schedule source in your ET-HOST radio chat.

The plugin does not require an ET-HOST account to manage or display schedules on your WordPress website.

An ET-HOST account and a compatible chat configuration are required to use the external schedule integration.

Updates are retrieved by ET-HOST according to its own caching and refresh behavior.

For more information about ET-HOST, visit:

https://et-host.de/

External services and privacy

MBrickz FM Schedule works independently within WordPress.

The plugin does not send data to external services, collect analytics, or transmit visitor information to third parties.

The frontend countdown and dynamic schedule features communicate with the WordPress website on which the plugin is installed.

If you choose to connect an external service such as ET-HOST, that service can retrieve the public JSON schedule endpoint.

The public REST endpoints expose published schedule information, including show titles, dates, times, presenter names, image URLs, and countdown-related timestamps.

Only publish information intended for public access.

No external service is required to use the schedule management, countdown, or frontend display features.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the mbrickz-fm-schedule folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin ZIP file through the WordPress plugin installer.
  2. Activate MBrickz FM Schedule through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Schedule > Add New Show.
  4. Enter the show title, description, date, start time, end time, presenter, and genre.
  5. Optionally select a show cover and presenter avatar from the media library.
  6. Publish the show.
  7. Add the [mbrickzfm_schedule] shortcode to a page or post.
  8. Customize the appearance under Schedule > Settings.
  9. Configure the desired pagination settings.
  10. Optionally enable the global countdown or add individual show countdown shortcodes to your website.

For external JSON integration, copy the endpoint URL displayed on the settings page.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin require an external radio service?

No. MBrickz FM Schedule can manage and display radio schedules independently of any external service.

Can I use the plugin with my existing WordPress theme?

Yes. The plugin uses its own responsive schedule and countdown layouts and inherits the frontend font family from your active theme.

Colors and border radii can be customized in the plugin settings.

The final appearance may also be affected by your theme’s styles.

Can I change the number of shows displayed per page?

Yes. Navigate to Schedule > Settings and configure the Shows per Page option in the Schedule Pagination section.

The default is five shows per page. Supported limits range from 1 to 100.

You can also override the global setting using the limit parameter in the shortcode.

For example:

[mbrickzfm_schedule limit="3"]

The limit only applies when pagination is enabled.

Can I disable pagination?

Yes. Disable the Pagination option under Schedule > Settings.

You can also disable pagination for an individual schedule shortcode:

[mbrickzfm_schedule pagination="false"]

This displays all available current and upcoming shows without pagination.

Can I override the global pagination settings?

Yes. Explicit shortcode parameters override the corresponding global plugin settings.

For example:

[mbrickzfm_schedule limit="3" pagination="true"]

This enables pagination and displays three shows per page, regardless of the global pagination settings.

Can I display a schedule on my homepage and another on my program page?

Yes. You can use the same shortcode with different parameters on different pages.

For example, display all available shows without pagination on your homepage and five shows per page on your program page.

Multiple paginated schedules on the same page currently share the same pagination URL parameter.

What happens to finished shows?

Finished shows are automatically excluded from the public schedule and JSON endpoint.

With JavaScript enabled, finished shows are automatically hidden from an already displayed schedule without requiring a full page reload.

The schedule and pagination are then refreshed in the background.

Finished shows remain available in the WordPress dashboard until you delete them.

Does pagination update when a show ends on another schedule page?

Yes. The frontend monitors the next scheduled show expiration across the entire schedule.

When a show ends, the schedule and pagination are refreshed, even if that show is not displayed on the currently selected page.

If the current page is no longer available, the last available schedule page is displayed automatically.

Does the live status require the global countdown to be enabled?

No. The automatic live status and schedule updates work independently of the global countdown setting.

Can I display a countdown without displaying the entire schedule?

Yes. Use the individual show countdown shortcode:

[fmsched_cnd id="123"]

Replace 123 with the ID of the desired radio show.

The individual countdown works independently of the main schedule and the global countdown setting.

Where can I find the ID of a radio show?

The radio show overview in the WordPress dashboard displays the ID of each show.

The overview also provides a copyable individual countdown shortcode for each show.

What happens to a countdown when a show begins?

The global countdown automatically switches to the next upcoming show, if one is available.

An individual countdown changes to a Live now display until the selected show ends.

What happens if no upcoming shows are available?

The global countdown is hidden when there are no upcoming shows.

If there are also no currently running shows, the schedule displays a message indicating that no upcoming shows are currently scheduled.

An individual countdown is hidden after its selected show ends.

Do countdowns use the visitor’s device clock?

Countdowns and automatic schedule status updates are synchronized with the WordPress server timestamp.

The frontend calculates elapsed time between server synchronization requests.

This reduces the dependency on the visitor’s device clock.

Is JavaScript required?

The initial schedule is rendered by WordPress and can be displayed without JavaScript.

JavaScript is required for automatically updating countdown values, switching live status indicators, and refreshing the schedule and pagination without a full page reload.

Does the plugin work with page caching?

The plugin uses server time synchronization and background requests to update countdowns and refresh the schedule.

However, page caching and REST API caching behavior depend on the caching system used by your website.

External caching systems may serve outdated schedule information or prevent timely background updates.

If you experience delayed or incorrect updates, review your caching configuration and consider excluding the schedule page and countdown REST endpoint from caching.

Are changes to show times immediately reflected on an already opened page?

Countdown information is synchronized with the server periodically.

The schedule uses the show timestamps available when the page was rendered or last refreshed.

Changes to scheduled broadcast times may therefore require a page refresh to be reflected immediately in the schedule.

Can I schedule a show that continues past midnight?

Yes. If the end time is earlier than the start time, the plugin treats the end time as occurring on the following day.

For example, a show starting at 22:30 and ending at 01:00 continues until the next calendar day.

External services may handle overnight shows differently.

What happens if the start and end times are identical?

Shows with identical start and end times are treated as invalid and are excluded from the public schedule and JSON endpoint.

Which timezone does the plugin use?

The plugin uses the timezone configured under Settings > General in WordPress.

We recommend selecting a named timezone, such as Europe/Berlin, rather than a fixed UTC offset, so that daylight saving time is handled automatically.

Can I prepare shows without displaying them publicly?

Yes. Save a show as a draft to prepare it without including it in the public schedule or JSON endpoint.

Only published shows with valid schedule information are displayed.

Does the plugin detect whether my radio stream is online?

No. The plugin manages scheduled radio shows.

The schedule status is based on the configured show date and times, not on the actual status of your audio stream.

A show marked as Live now is scheduled to be running at that time. This does not confirm that a live broadcast is taking place.

Does the plugin include an audio player?

No. MBrickz FM Schedule is a radio schedule management plugin and does not provide audio streaming or playback functionality.

Do the JSON REST endpoints require authentication?

No. The endpoints are intentionally public and read-only so that the frontend and compatible external services can retrieve published schedule information.

They do not provide an interface for creating, editing, or deleting shows.

Does frontend pagination affect the JSON schedule endpoint?

No. The JSON schedule endpoint returns all valid current and upcoming published shows, regardless of the shortcode’s limit or pagination settings.

Is the plugin available in German?

Yes. English is the default language, and German translations are available through WordPress.org.

The displayed language follows your WordPress site or administration language settings.

What happens to my data when I uninstall the plugin?

By default, all radio shows and plugin settings are retained when the plugin is deleted.

If you want to permanently remove all plugin data, enable the “Delete all plugin data on uninstall” option under Schedule > Settings before deleting the plugin.

This removes all radio shows, associated metadata, revisions, and plugin settings, including design, countdown, and pagination settings.

Images and other files in the WordPress media library are not deleted.

Deactivating the plugin does not remove any data.
sections.changelog:
0.2.0

  • Added an optional global countdown to the next upcoming radio show.
  • Added individual show countdowns using the [fmsched_cnd id=”123″] shortcode.
  • Added countdown display with days, hours, minutes, and seconds.
  • Added automatic singular and plural countdown unit labels.
  • Added automatic transitions from individual countdowns to live status displays.
  • Added automatic switching of the global countdown to the next upcoming show.
  • Added server-synchronized countdowns through a dedicated REST API endpoint.
  • Added show IDs and copyable individual countdown shortcodes to the dashboard show overview.
  • Added a sortable show ID column.
  • Added automatic Live now indicators to running show cards.
  • Added a subtle pulsing red live status indicator.
  • Added support for reduced motion preferences.
  • Added automatic hiding of finished shows without a full page reload.
  • Added dynamic schedule and pagination updates after scheduled shows end.
  • Added schedule-wide expiration monitoring across all pagination pages.
  • Added automatic fallback to the last available schedule page when necessary.
  • Added global settings for pagination and the number of shows per page.
  • Added shortcode overrides for global pagination settings.
  • Changed disabled pagination to display all available shows, regardless of the limit parameter.
  • Added improved validation of pagination settings and shortcode parameters.
  • Extended the uninstallation routine to remove countdown and pagination settings when requested.
  • Maintained compatibility with the existing JSON schedule endpoint and ET-HOST integration.

0.1.1

  • Removed directory-only assets and bundled translation files from the plugin package.
  • Removed unnecessary manual text domain loading.
  • Fixed unexpected output during plugin activation.

  • Initial release.
  • Added dedicated radio show management.
  • Added show date, start time, end time, presenter, and genre fields.
  • Added show cover and presenter avatar support.
  • Added support for shows continuing past midnight.
  • Added responsive frontend schedule shortcode.
  • Added chronological sorting and configurable pagination.
  • Added automatic exclusion of finished and invalid shows.
  • Added customizable colors and border radii.
  • Added design reset functionality.
  • Added enhanced dashboard show overview with sortable columns.
  • Added schedule status indicators.
  • Added live preview in the radio show editor.
  • Added automatic redirect to the show overview after publishing.
  • Added public JSON REST API for compatible external services.
  • Added English and German language support.
  • Added optional plugin data removal on uninstall.
